reviews.author: nadia-sec
reviews.body:
Not leaving this on a line because it is about the change as a whole rather than any one of them.

This caches an authorization decision for ten minutes with no invalidation path. When an admin is demoted, or a member is removed from the org entirely, every gateway process that already resolved them keeps serving the old permission set until the entry expires. That is a ten minute window where a revoked user still passes an authorization check, and the offboarding runbook we hand customers says access ends immediately.

The TTL is not the fix; a shorter one narrows the window without closing it. This needs an explicit invalidation on the grant-change path, or the decision needs to stay uncached. I do not think this should go out as it stands.

reviews.author: petra-dev
reviews.body: Cache mechanics look right to me and the tests cover the lifetime. Approving on that basis.

comments.author: rhodes-dev
comments.body: Rebased on main to pick up the cache-key change from #311.

comments.author: petra-dev
comments.body: Numbers from the staging soak are in the ticket if anyone wants them.

comments.author: tobin-sre
comments.body: We ran almost exactly this cache in billing last year and could not tell for six weeks whether it was doing anything, because nothing exported a hit rate. Please add hit/miss counters before this ships, otherwise the first question in the next latency incident is one we cannot answer.

comments.author: quill-bot
comments.body: `_cache.get` returning `None` is ambiguous if a resolve can legitimately return `None`.

comments.author: rhodes-dev
comments.body: It cannot; `_resolve_uncached` returns an empty frozenset for no permissions, never `None`. Added that to the docstring so the next reader does not have to check.

comments.author: petra-dev
comments.body: If this shares an eviction pool with the feature-flag cache, a burst of permission entries will evict flags and we will get flag flapping under load.

comments.author: rhodes-dev
comments.body: Good catch. Made it a second instance with its own cap rather than a shared pool, so the two cannot evict each other.

comments.author: petra-dev
comments.body: Worth asserting the org passed through here is the same one the request authenticated against, not the one in the path parameter.

comments.author: rhodes-dev
comments.body: It is the authenticated one; the path parameter never reaches this call. Added a test that a mismatched path org does not change the cache key.
